searchText: Do we really want to reject this? If we keep `JUMP` in EOF, then it would make sense that `PC` is also still available. Also regarding the terminating opcodes; if `RJUMP` is at the end of the code container and this jump is valid, then this should also be a valid terminating opcode I'd say? I am also not sure what happens in `RJUMPV` if `case > 255`. The EIP is not clear about it. Do we do the default branch (so just move to the pc post instruction), or do we throw and consume all gas? EIP-4750 removes `JUMP` & `JUMPI` from EOF. Anyhow, I don't mind keeping PC valid in EOF, I just find "Note: EIP-3670 should reject PC" confusing and advocate its removal from EIP-4200. Yes, I agree, either you must remove it or not, but not "should" remove it If JUMP and JUMPI get removed I guess that there is no real need for PC anymore, but maybe there are some smart tricks you could use, so I would say do not remove it (an use case I can think of is that if you are at a PUSH opcode, which PUSHs exactly the current `PC` on stack, you can golf the code by replacing the PUSH by PC (this saves code deposit gas) and `PC` is 2 gas, where `PUSH` is 3 gas). So I would say to not remove it To deprecate `CALLCODE` (not sure if this is in any of the EOF EIPs) I would agree to it It was just loosely suggested to drop `PC` to limit the observability of the code position. But this is not a planned change any more. The `PC` stays as a fancy constant push. This is exactly the case with EIP-5450. And the reason we are removing the "terminating instruction" case from EIP-3670. If your runtime index is out of the number of cases the control flow falls though to the next instruction. This is specified by `PC_post_instruction + ((case >= (count + 1)) ? 0 : relative_offset[case])`. Although, I'd say `case > count` 😉 Should the "but it also allows the deprecation of the `PC` instruction." stay? I think it should be removed, there might be fancy use cases we are not aware of and I think it should be motivated why it allows for deprecation of PC. I'm not sure here because if I have `case` 257 then the code would evaluate to `relative_offset[256]` (zero-indexed table) which is not defined..? And your equation is not in the EIP currently, it is `PC_post_instruction + ((case >= count) ? 0 : relative_offset[case])` currently So `256` is a case which should be defined right? Then this would get `relative_offset[255]` (if we use zero-indexed lists)? https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/6111 Ah wait I'm reading this one wrong, you are right, this one is correct, now it makes sense 🙂 But this should be `PC_post_instruction + ((case >= (count + 1)) ? 0 : relative_offset[case - 1]).` right? The reference code seems to be python, and since it is zero indexed then I would argue that the case should thus also be `case - 1`? PUSH should cost 2 😉 `CALLCODE` is deprecated in EIP-3670: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3670#specification Ah cool 🙂 We should update our implementation of 3670 then because we do not yet have it Sorry, I was looking at the previous version of the EIP. So to clarify `count` is the length of the `relative_offset` array. The array is 0-indexed. And the `case` is the index. So the `case >= count` is the out-of-bounds condition and then control flow just goes to the next instruction: `PC_post_instruction + 0`. Ah right sorry, you are again right, I keep reading this `a : b ? c` syntax the wrong way 🙂 Now I also see the point made about the `ISZERO JUMPI` stuff 🙂 https://github.com/ethereumjs/ethereumjs-monorepo/pull/2446 I'm implementing it here 🙂
